clue.text: Substance producing effect, bringing about 15 3

indicators.note: bringing something about suggests turning it around and remaking it, so the letters of the cross-referenced phrase are reordered

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the theme phrase at 15 across and 3 down, the warming of the planet

explanation.surface: A warning that some pollutant is what causes global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the whole answer to 15 and 3, CLIMATE CHANGE, whose thirteen letters are rearranged by 'bringing about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound used to produce a particular effect, such as a nerve gas or defoliant, is the standard term for this.

clue.text: See 24 across
See 15
Send down rook, queen half hidden

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle them, so a con

indicators.note: with half of the name out of sight only its front half shows

parts.note: Victoria is the famous British queen

explanation.surface: A chess note: a rook is played to send the queen down, with the queen partly blocked from view.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess terms mislead: 'rook' is a verb meaning cheat, and the queen is a monarch, VICTORIA, of which only VICT is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To send down is British slang for sentencing someone to prison, which follows a guilty verdict.

clue.text: Not quite everything contained by flood barriers after a rise — in this?

indicators.note: one piece sits within the walls of another, so it goes inside
in a down clue, a word that has risen reads from bottom to top, so it is written backwards

parts.note: levees are embankments built to hold back a river in flood

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Floodwalls are needed once the waters have risen, and the clue asks where that rise happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: the rise the surface talks about happens in this. 'after a rise' looks like the timing of the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise that threatens coasts as the climate warms is measured as the mean height of the ocean surface.

clue.text: Capable of grasping vacuous ideas, help ne'er arranged

indicators.note: letters arranged are put into a new order
vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its inside letters, leaving only its outer pair

explanation.surface: Someone able to grasp hollow notions, helped by nobody, is drawn as a mind that clutches at empty ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous ideas' gives IS, the outer letters of IDEAS; with HELPNEER these ten letters are 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail or limb that can wrap around and hold things, as a monkey's tail does, is described with this zoological term.

clue.text: Very much that's heartbreaking with empty pockets, oh my Lord!

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, keeping just the first and last letters

parts.note: the word with, emptied of its middle letters, leaves its outer pair
a ton is informal for a great deal
read as heart breaking: the word heart broken up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry of despair at something heartbreaking happening to someone who is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartbreaking' splits as heart breaking, an anagram inside one word. 'pockets' does not fit the order cleanly: the parse needs the emptied 'with' to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonishment or exasperation, used interchangeably in speech.

clue.text: Something online for minors, I say, drinking liquor

indicators.note: one piece takes the other in as if swallowing a drink, so it goes inside

parts.note: coo is a mild British exclamation of surprise, like I say
hooch is slang for strong or illicit liquor

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something on the internet for underage users who are drinking alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' misleads: the definition means something running on a railway line, a nursery word for children ('minors').
explanation.definitionFit: This is a child's word for a steam train, which runs on a line.

clue.text: See 7
Warning of mass extinction, now all kicking off

indicators.note: each of the words kicks off, so the start of every word is taken

explanation.surface: A dire warning that mass extinction is now beginning everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or sign of what is to come, often bad, serves as a warning.

clue.text: Something sinister locked in extremes of nature for post-apocalyptic writer

indicators.note: the pieces go in between the outer letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: evil is something wicked or sinister
shut means locked

explanation.surface: Some menace is caged within nature's extremes, as told by a novelist of the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The English-Australian novelist wrote On the Beach, about the last survivors of a nuclear war.

clue.text: Light bracket formerly placed behind sack, oddly

indicators.note: the second piece goes after the first
oddly means the odd-numbered letters, the first and third

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A light-hearted note about a bracket that used to be put behind a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a candle holder or light fitting fixed to a wall by a bracket.

clue.text: Punched by Mafia's leader, Irishman doubled up is an informer

indicators.note: doubled means the result is written twice
in a down clue, up means the letters are read backwards
a word punched by a letter has that letter driven into it

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Irishman beaten by the Mafia boss, bent double, turns out to be a grass.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes into SEAN for SEMAN, reversed by 'up' to NAMES, then 'doubled'. 'doubled up' looks like pain from the punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify accomplices to the police or authorities is what an informer does.

clue.text: Relative bound by fancy contract

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to fancy something is to covet it
nan is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member tied into an elaborate agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal binding agreement or promise, such as a deed restricting land use, is a type of contract.

clue.text: Terrible mistake detailed about one reaching end of game, extreme temperatures — with this?

indicators.note: the outer piece goes about the inner ones, surrounding them
de-tailed, with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a clanger is a British word for a howling blunder
one is the Roman numeral I
mate is checkmate, the end of a game of chess
C and H are the cold and hot taps, the extremes of temperature

explanation.surface: A disastrous blunder about someone finishing a game, then a question about scorching weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts CLANGER to CLANGE, which goes 'about' I, MATE and CH. The definition leans on the rest: extreme temperatures come with this.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term shifts in global weather patterns bring heatwaves and cold snaps more often.

clue.text: Social affair thus far coming up, cut by a fraction

indicators.note: one piece is split open with the other inserted
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: yet means thus far, up to now
a part is a fraction of a whole

explanation.surface: A gathering so far on the rise, then trimmed by a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon gathering where tea and cakes are served is a sociable occasion.

clue.text: Figure is covering page in magazine

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the magazine

parts.note: Elle is a well-known fashion magazine

indicators.note: a word covering a letter holds it inside

explanation.surface: A figure is shown hiding a page in a magazine, perhaps a model on a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an oval geometric shape, a plane curve, so a figure in geometry.

clue.text: Hackney's condition is surprising

definitions.meaning: a hackney is a breed of horse, and this word names an illness of horses that makes them unsteady
a verb meaning astonishes or amazes

explanation.surface: The state of Hackney, the London borough, is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough; it is the horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease makes horses lurch and reel; the verb means amazes, as in 'it staggers belief'.

clue.text: Bang on about Italian author's good manners

indicators.note: the outer piece goes about the inner one

parts.note: to drum is to bang on something
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: Someone banging on about an Italian writer's courtesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' looks like 'exactly right'; it is to beat a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper behaviour and propriety in social situations is the formal word for etiquette.

clue.text: Ballet move: sweep featuring sliding over of booty

indicators.note: one piece contains the other as a feature

parts.note: to sweep along is to glide

indicators.note: a word that slides over is flipped, read the other way

parts.note: booty is slang for the backside, an ass

explanation.surface: A ballet move: a sweep that features a dancer sliding over on the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gliding step in ballet, one foot sliding out followed by the other.

clue.text: Promoting toilet humour ultimately, Paul regularly immature

indicators.note: promoted pieces are moved up, and in a down clue that reads them backwards

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter
regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Paul admits that pushing lavatory humour is childish.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter names himself; 'Promoting' turns LAVRAL upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva is the young stage of an insect, so this adjective means undeveloped.

clue.text: In fiendish Satan's triumph, hope's ending for God

indicators.note: one letter is placed in among the others
fiendish means wild or devilish, so the letters are scrambled
the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: As the devil triumphs, all hope ends for the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of 'hope' is the letter used, hope's ending; it goes 'In' the anagram of SATANSTRIUMPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular informal name for the deity, the figure who lives above in heaven.

clue.text: Belief in 22 26 is hard in worrying times

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the rearranged letters
worrying means troubling or shaking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Faith in God is hard to hold in anxious times.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is the belief in the existence of a deity, the one above in heaven.

clue.text: Parched, so a brandy mixed with last of lemonade

indicators.note: a drink mixed has its ingredients stirred together, so the letters are reordered
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail: a brandy mixed with the dregs of lemonade for someone thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means completely without moisture, extremely thirsty or dried out.

clue.text: Critical time off: no, quite the opposite

parts.note: food that is off has gone high, smelly
the preceding word turned around, the reverse of no read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is a crucial break, and replies no, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite the opposite' supplies the preceding 'no' read in reverse. 'off' means rotten, as of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday showdown, from the western film, is an idiom for a decisive moment of confrontation.

clue.text: With gas on, a temperature warmer?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Turning the gas on, a heater raises the temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: what warms is heat, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth itself, the thing that makes something hotter, is a loose description of heat.
